customerJourneyStories.name: From a patchwork of tools to Logic4
customerJourneyStories.summary: An owner whose webshop, stock list and accounting no longer keep up chooses Logic4 as the single system.

stages.narrative: A peak season ends with overselling, late invoices and staff copying orders between the webshop and the accounting package; the owner decides the tools must be replaced.
The owner hears about Logic4 from a supplier or branch association peer, sees it at a trade fair or finds it comparing 'ERP met webshop' packages online.

A demo with the company's own assortment; comparison with Exact plus a separate webshop and with Odoo; checking the Smart versus Business package, implementation effort and references in the same branch.
A bounded implementation: item and customer migration, one webshop and the order desk go live first while the old shop runs until cut-over.
Weekly dashboard review becomes routine; a second label shop and marketplace connections via EffectConnect follow on the same back office.
The owner stays because updates are free and the system keeps growing with the company; upgrades to Professional for multi-warehouse and EDI rather than switching vendor.

One label goes live on the Logic4 webshop with the full assortment while the old shop stays up for the other label.
Edits banners and content daily, launches campaigns from the CMS, and connects bol and Amazon through EffectConnect.
Stays because stock and prices are always right and adding a new shop takes days, not a project; requests features through the Logic4 customer channel.

customerJourneyStories.name: Adopting the Logic4 order desk and B2B portal
customerJourneyStories.summary: A sales team moves quoting from spreadsheets to Logic4 and opens a B2B portal for its accounts.

stages.narrative: A key account complains about wrong prices on two invoices in one month; quotes still live in spreadsheets.
Sales hears about the B2B portal from the e-commerce manager and from a peer dealer using Logic4.
Tests quoting with real price agreements and staffel discounts in the demo; checks that portal prices equal quote prices.
Quotes for one sales rep run in Logic4 for a month; ten friendly accounts get portal logins.
All quotes run in Logic4; follow-up tasks come from the pipeline; accounts reorder through quick-order lists.
The team stays because account history, prices and orders are in one place; asks for EDI for the largest customers.

customerJourneyStories.name: From paper pick lists to the Logic4 warehouse app
customerJourneyStories.summary: A warehouse lead replaces paper pick lists with location-based scanning in Logic4.

stages.narrative: Two customers receive the same parcel twice in one week because paper pick lists were printed twice.
The lead sees the warehouse app in the Logic4 implementation plan and hears about it from a peer warehouse using it.
Tests scanners on the warehouse floor, checks location setup effort and carrier label printing; compares with Picqer as a dedicated WMS.
One zone is labelled with locations and picked with scanners for two weeks while the rest stays on paper.
All picking runs on scanners; count reminders become a weekly routine; labels print automatically at packing.
Stays because errors dropped and stock is trusted; when volumes exceed built-in WMS, Picqer is added as a Katapull option without changing the ERP.

stages.narrative: A supplier price increase is missed for a month and dozens of orders ship below cost.
The purchaser learns in the Logic4 implementation that branch article databases can be imported directly.
Checks which supplier and branch databases are supported, how matching works and how price rules apply margins.
Imports one supplier's assortment and runs min/max suggestions for one category.
All supplier price files update automatically; weekly suggestion runs replace spreadsheets; new items go live in days.
Stays because data quality and margins are under control; asks for EDI purchase orders and demand-based levels.

customerJourneyStories.name: Bringing branches onto one cloud POS
customerJourneyStories.summary: A store manager moves from a standalone register to Logic4's multi-branch cloud POS.

stages.narrative: Prices at the register differ from the webshop and a customer leaves after a dispute.
Head office announces Logic4 POS as part of the ERP roll-out; the manager visits a sister branch already live.
Checks speed at the register, terminal integration, offline behaviour and how branch bookkeeping stays separate; compares with keeping Vendit or Lightspeed POS.
One register runs Logic4 POS for two weeks next to the old one.
All registers run Logic4; reservations from other branches become routine; cash-up takes minutes.
Stays because prices and customers are shared and branch books post automatically.
